newsitem.title: USA: US FERC eases electricity open access waiver rules.
newsitem.headline: US FERC eases electricity open access waiver rules.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on Tuesday eased its criteria for granting waivers from its open access transmission and electricity information rules.

Under the looser standard, utilities which owned or operated limited transmission facilities that were not part of an integrated power grid would not be required to file a tariff offering other power producers the same rate as it charged itself.
Also under the new standard, the same utilities would not be required to set up a computer system to publicize its available transmission capacity.
However, if a utility with a waiver received a request for service in the future, it would have to file an open access tariff within 60 days.
FERC said utilities that sell less than 4 million megawatt-hours a year would not have to set up an open electronic information system unless it was part of a highly-integrated power pool.
Under the new criteria, the commission granted open access waivers to two electric cooperatives.

It issued waivers from the information rule to several small utilities, but denied waivers to three members of the New England Pool -- Bangor Hydro-Electric Co, United Illuminating Co and Citizens Utilities.
It also denied a waiver request on the information requirements from Central Illinois Public Service Co pending the company's proposed merger with Union Electric Co.
